affects.why: Strong data raises the odds of the 9 Dec Fed hike markets already expect (Forbes); higher rate odds have weighed on gold this month (Trading Economics).

calendar.beat_record: A miss of 100k+ typically moves the S&P 500 0.5–1.5% and the dollar about 0.5% in the first hour; unemployment, wages and revisions can reverse it (FinanceCalendar).
downside: A strong number would firm up the December hike that is already 84% priced (FedWatch via Yardeni).
calendar.expected: About +59,000 jobs (forecasts 50,000 Barclays to 95,000 RSM); unemployment steady at 4.2%; Deutsche Bank sees wages +0.3% (Kiplinger). September added only 29k. Reuters poll (6 Nov): about +65,000 (range 35k–125k), unemployment 4.2%, wages +0.3% m/m and 2.9% y/y, the first sub-3% annual reading since May 2021.
calendar.priced: Prediction markets (14 Oct) put the median at about +55k jobs, range -10k to +125k.

result.headline: Much stronger than expected: +165,000 jobs, unemployment 4.1%
points: Payrolls +165,000 vs about 65,000 expected; September revised up to 60,000 (Kitco).
Unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%; hourly pay +0.4% m/m vs 0.3% forecast, 3.1% y/y.
Strengthens the case for a December Fed hike; 2-year yields rose about 6bp to 4.53%.
Gold fell about 1%; Nasdaq still closed up 1.09% as chip stocks bounced (TheStreet).

upside: A weak number would lower the odds of the December Fed hike; falling December odds support gold and shares (Admirals).

calendar.beat_record: Zacks ESP +8.2%; average EPS surprise 23% over the last two quarters. EBITDA beat in 4 of 5 quarters, revenue missed in 4 of 5 (TIKR).
downside: The Texas governor-elect wants a data-centre moratorium; KeyBanc downgraded Vistra to Sector Weight on 4 Nov, saying it has the greatest exposure (Investing.com).
2027 revenue consensus cut ~4% since June; weaker Texas power forward prices; BMO cut its target to $210 (TIKR).
Texas holds about a quarter of US data-centre capacity due by 2030, and the new governor-elect ousted Abbott (Reuters).
calendar.expected: EPS ~$2.71–2.89, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.1bn (TIKR); 2026 EBITDA guidance $6.8–7.6bn reaffirmed. Revenue estimates vary widely ($6.7–7.8bn). Results before the US open, call 3pm UK. MarketBeat consensus: EPS $3.01, revenue $6.03bn; average analyst target $202.43. Zacks consensus: EPS $2.34, revenue $7.44bn; Zacks ESP +7.5% points to a likely beat.
means: Judge Vistra on adjusted EBITDA, not EPS: its EPS jumps around with hedging accounting. About $2.1bn is expected (TIKR).
It beat EBITDA forecasts in 5 of the 6 quarters with a forecast, yet the shares fell after 5 of the last 8 reports.
The call matters more than the quarter: management will update 2026 and 2027 guidance, and the CFO says 2027 is trending to the low end of $7.4-7.8bn.
Upside: the Meta nuclear deals and the Cogentrix purchase could add about $700m to 2027, and a government nuclear loan of up to $4.2bn is pending.
Options price about 8.3% either way (as of 3 Nov), well above its 5.3% 10-year average move (earnings-watcher).
You hold it for a few months, so this report sits inside your window.
past_notes: Q4 24: fell 12.3% on a day when AI and power stocks sold off broadly.
Q2 25: missed on EBITDA, fell 7% before the open, then closed up 2.4%.
calendar.priced: Options imply ±8–11%, about double its 10-year average (±5.3%); the actual move beat the implied move in only 4 of 18 reports.

result.headline: Beat on EBITDA and EPS, revenue missed; shares closed +10.55% at $124.80 (confirmed)
points: Adjusted EBITDA (ongoing ops) $2.38bn vs ~$2.1bn expected, up over 50% on a year ago (Vistra, TIKR).
Adjusted EPS $3.01 vs $2.71 consensus; revenue $6.35bn missed the $6.79bn expected (XTB).
2026 EBITDA guidance narrowed to $7.1–7.5bn with a higher midpoint; first 2027 range $7.7–8.5bn, above the $7.4–7.8bn the CFO had flagged; $1.5bn more buybacks.
Shares closed up 10.55% at $124.80 (StockAnalysis) from Thursday's 52-week low; XTB says investors focused on future cash flow, with about 98% of 2027 output hedged.
For your few-months holding: the report removed the near-term guidance-cut worry, though the stock is still well below its $203.66 high.

upside: The DOE nuclear loan (up to $4.2bn) and a 2026/27 guidance update on the call (TIKR).
calendar.watch_line: Shares fell 13.8% and then 6.2% into the report (to $112.87); options imply ±12.7% (earnings-watcher, 5 Nov).

affects.why: Hot inflation lifted rate-hike odds, which pushed gold to its lowest since July this week (Trading Economics).

calendar.beat_record: Treasury yields usually rise on a hot print and fall on a soft one (TickerVelocity).
downside: A hot print lifts yields; growth shares can suffer while financials outperform (TickerVelocity).
calendar.expected: Monthly: +0.3% headline and +0.2% core expected (FXEmpire, 8 Nov); RBC expects +0.3% / +0.3%; Cleveland Fed nowcast +0.24% / +0.21%. No yearly rate will be published for overall or core prices because October 2025 data were never collected. September: +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y.
calendar.priced: Markets price an 84% chance of a December Fed hike (CME FedWatch via Investing.com, 10 Nov), so a hot print mainly confirms it; a soft print would be the surprise.

result.headline: Hotter than expected: +0.4% headline and +0.3% core, both 0.1 point above forecasts
points: Headline prices rose 0.4% in the month vs 0.3% expected (September was +0.6%); core, which strips out food and energy, rose 0.3% vs 0.2% expected (Yahoo Finance).
Food rose 0.5% and energy 0.7%; no yearly rate was published because October 2025 data were never collected (Yahoo Finance).
Rate-hike bets firmed: CME FedWatch showed 90% odds of a quarter-point December hike and 10% for a half-point (Kiplinger).
Yields jumped (2-year +18.9bp to 4.74%, 10-year 4.99%) and the Nasdaq fell 0.74%; gold dropped about 2.6% (Kiplinger, Trading Economics).
For you: this matches the 'hot print' case in the preview: growth shares and gold (SGLN -1.6%) fell, while VWRP had already closed in London before the US slide.

upside: A soft print would pull yields down, which helps long-duration growth shares (TickerVelocity).

affects.why: Sterling traders are looking ahead to Thursday's Q3 GDP report after the pound fell 0.8% to $1.333 today (Trading Economics); a weaker pound raises the sterling value of VWRP's overseas shares.

calendar.expected: Third-quarter GDP is expected to show 0.7% growth (Trading Economics, 10 Nov).

result.headline: Stronger than expected: September +0.2% vs 0.0% forecast; Q3 +0.7% as expected
points: Q3 GDP grew 0.7% (Q2 0.5%), matching the 0.7% Trading Economics forecast; 1.9% higher than a year earlier (ONS).
September grew 0.2% vs 0.0% expected; August revised down to 0.0% (ONS, InvestingLive).
Services led (+0.9% over the quarter) while construction fell 0.7% (ONS).
InvestingLive says the resilient growth keeps a December BoE hike on track.
For you: VWRP rose 0.28% today; a firmer pound would trim the sterling value of its overseas shares.

calendar.expected: +0.4% month on month (September +1.3%), 6.6% year on year (September 6.3%), core +0.3% m/m. A 6.6% yearly rise would be the highest since November 2022 (StockTitan).
calendar.priced: About a 90% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike on 9 Dec in CME FedWatch; this is the last CPI/PPI print before that meeting (StockTitan).

affects.why: Nvidia is the All-World fund's largest holding at 5.0% (Vanguard).
First report without Huang; Nvidia says roadmap and customer commitments continue without interruption (Nvidia 8-K).

calendar.beat_record: Beat EPS in 7 of the last 8 quarters (MarketBeat).
downside: Huang resigned on 12 Nov; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and a permanent search is under way (Nvidia 8-K). Shares closed at $166.19 after a $148.80 low (CoinDesk).
WSJ reported on 11 Nov the board is preparing to oust Huang; shares fell about 8% after hours to around $160 (Yahoo Finance, StockTitan).
Three customers are 44% of revenue; purchase commitments up to $279bn; gross margin guided lower; no China data-centre sales assumed (XTB).
The board opened an independent probe on 8 Nov into reports Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence; House chairs want a briefing on 18 Nov (NBC, FourWeekMBA).
Trump said on 9 Nov the FBI is looking into Huang's relationship with the alleged spy, though he said he believes Huang (Al Jazeera).
calendar.expected: EPS $2.49, revenue $108.8bn (MarketBeat), just above Nvidia's own $108bn ±2% guide; gross margin guided 74%.

history_sources.name: Regards of Wall Street NVDA earnings moves

key_metrics.why: Beating its own guide is expected
Historically the main driver of the move

means: Nvidia guided $108bn revenue and a 74% gross margin; the consensus ($108.8bn) is only just above its own guide.
It beat in 7 of the last 8 quarters but the shares fell after 5 of them. What moves it is the outlook for the next quarter, not the beat.
Last quarter it rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts. That is the pattern to look for.
Its results also move your grid ETF and your Vanguard fund, where Nvidia is one of the largest holdings.
past_notes: Q1 FY26: EPS shown as a miss only because of a $4.5bn China export charge; underlying EPS $0.96 beat.
Q2 FY27 (Aug): rose 8.7% after guiding well above forecasts.

previews.name: Bernstein downgrade to Market Perform, target $200, 12 Nov (Yahoo Finance)

calendar.priced: Options not yet listed for the event. Its 10-year average results move is ±8.4% (2-year ±5.7%); last quarter options implied ±5.9% and it closed +8.7%.
upside: Last quarter's guide was well above consensus, and the CFO pointed to ~70% growth in FY28 vs ~44% expected (XTB).
calendar.watch_line: Watch: whether Huang is still CEO, next quarter's revenue guide and gross margin

affects.why: Lawmakers want answers on Huang's ties to a businesswoman US officials call a Chinese intelligence asset (ABC News).

calendar.event: House committee chairs' requested closed-door briefing with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (Huang resigned as CEO on 12 Nov)
calendar.expected: Three House committee chairs asked for a briefing on 18 Nov; Rep. Brian Mast said he is prepared to subpoena Huang if he does not respond (ABC News).

affects.why: Google is investing $10bn in a $26bn private sale of non-voting stock at the IPO price (TechCrunch).
Nvidia is also investing $10bn in that private sale (TechCrunch).

calendar.event: Anthropic IPO expected to start trading (Nasdaq: ANT)
calendar.expected: Price range $70-78 a share, up to $64.4bn raised and up to $1.4tn valuation (Fortune).

calendar.beat_record: Beat EPS in each of the last 4 quarters.
downside: Current bookings growth (cRPO) slowed to 12% from 18–20% and is expected to stay lower for several quarters; full-year guide midpoint was below consensus.
calendar.expected: Autodesk's own guide: revenue $2.125–2.140bn, non-GAAP EPS $3.04–3.09. Consensus ~$3.14 (Earnings Whispers).

key_metrics.why: It has beaten its guide every quarter here
Future contracted revenue: the market's worry
Cuts here would hit the shares

means: Autodesk beat forecasts in all 8 of the last quarters, but the shares rose after only 4.
In its last two reports it beat yet fell about 4% each time, because full-year guidance came in light and future contracted revenue (cRPO) slowed to 12% growth from 18-20%.
So the key numbers are cRPO and the free-cash-flow guide ($2.725-2.750bn for the year), not the EPS beat.
You hold it for a few months, so this report falls inside your holding window.
past_notes: Q1 and Q2 FY27: beat both times, but fell ~4% each time on light guidance and slowing cRPO.
calendar.priced: Options not yet listed. Last quarter implied ±9.4%; its 10-year average move is ±8.5% (2-year ±7.8%).
calendar.time: after US close (estimate; not yet confirmed)
upside: Subscription revenue grew 17% last quarter vs 14.5% expected; BofA calls second-half guidance conservative (Finviz).
calendar.watch_line: Watch: cRPO growth and full-year guidance

affects.why: Hearing follows reports that a network linked to Alice Huang moved about 240,000 restricted Nvidia chips into China (Asia Times, citing The Information).

calendar.expected: Chair Tim Scott invited Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify; House Foreign Affairs chair Brian Mast also said a subpoena would follow if necessary (Newsweek).

stories.headline: Reuters reports a third relationship involving Jensen Huang; Senate Banking chair invites him to a 3 Dec hearing

impacts.why: Shares fell 14% at Thursday's open, recovered about half and closed down 4.3%, after already falling 27% from October's record (source 1).

sources.title: Jensen Huang Reportedly Had Third Affair; Nvidia Exit Caps Week of Scandal
Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO

stories.summary: After Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar, that he had a relationship with a second Nvidia employee, the third attributed to him. Nvidia did not comment. Senate Banking chair Tim Scott invited Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick to a public hearing on 3 December and warned subpoenas could follow; Harvey Jones is now board chair and the board will look at internal and external CEO candidates.

explainer.meaning: Renting computing power on chips sitting in another country's data centre, which lets a company use banned chips without importing them.

stories.headline: US said to be finalising a rule blocking Chinese firms from renting advanced AI chips in overseas data centres

impacts.why: Nvidia reportedly told cloud partners at least 51% of new business should go to non-Chinese customers; Asia Times says the US rule would be stricter (source 1). Chinese firms had placed over $35bn of Nvidia orders, per Reuters (source 2).

sources.title: Huang's fall, US curbs put China's AI computing in peril
Alibaba Sinks 8% on Report U.S. Is Finalizing Curbs on China's Remote AI Chip Access

stories.summary: The Information reported the Commerce Department is close to a rule that would require export licences for Blackwell-class chips in data centres in places like Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Brazil when Chinese-linked firms use them. US-run data centres there would be exempt if they block access from China. Alibaba fell about 8% and Baidu 4% on the report; the Hang Seng Tech index fell 2.4% overnight.

explainer.meaning: The networking gear, servers and chips that data centres buy to run AI, a sign of how much big tech is spending.

stories.headline: Cisco beats and raises guidance; sees AI infrastructure revenue more than doubling to $9bn this fiscal year

sources.title: Cisco beats expectations, lifts guidance and forecasts AI infrastructure revenue to double in fiscal 2027

stories.summary: Cisco's quarterly revenue rose 24% to $18.5bn against $18.1bn expected, with adjusted EPS of $1.40 vs $1.33. Next-quarter guidance of $18.0-18.2bn revenue topped the $17.88bn forecast, and it raised its fiscal 2027 AI infrastructure revenue forecast to $9bn. Shares were flat in late trading after a 32% gain this year.

explainer.meaning: Gold pays no interest, so when bond yields and the dollar rise, holding gold looks less attractive and its price tends to fall.

stories.headline: Gold steadies near $3,880 after hitting a one-year low below $3,860 as the dollar reaches an 18-month high

impacts.why: SGLN tracks gold, which hit a one-year low below $3,860 on Thursday (source 1).

sources.title: US PPI in Focus as Gold Falls Below $3,900, Dollar Rallies and Nvidia Shock Hits Wall Street

stories.summary: Gold fell as much as 3.4% on Thursday to below $3,860 an ounce, its lowest in a year, before steadying near $3,880-3,884 this morning. The dollar index is near 103.2, close to a 19-month high, as markets expect the Fed to raise rates in December. Traders are watching today's US producer price data.

impacts.why: About 60% of VWRP is US shares; US futures were up 0.4-0.6% this morning (source 1).

sources.title: The PPI Report Comes Friday, With Economists Expecting a 6.6% Yearly Rise
US PPI in Focus as Gold Falls Below $3,900, Dollar Rallies and Nvidia Shock Hits Wall Street

stories.summary: Economists expect October PPI to rise 0.4% on the month after September's 1.3% jump, taking the yearly rate to 6.6%, the highest since November 2022. Core is seen up 0.3%. Futures give about a 90% chance of a quarter-point Fed hike in December, and the US 10-year yield is above 5%.

explainer.meaning: The main global benchmark price for oil, used to price most of the world's supply.

stories.headline: Oil jumps 3.3% to just over $94 a barrel after Trump says the US does not need a deal with Iran
stories.summary: Brent crude rose about 3.3% to just over $94, reversing Wednesday's fall. Higher oil feeds into inflation, which is behind expectations of further rate rises from the Fed and Bank of England.

stories.summary: Sterling traded just below $1.33, down 0.07%, despite UK Q3 growth of 0.7%. The dollar is supported by expectations of further Fed tightening and hawkish Fed comments.

The US is reportedly finalising a rule to stop Chinese firms renting advanced AI chips in overseas data centres; Hong Kong tech fell 2.4%.
